We partnered with artist Prune Nourry on a documentary film that uses Google AI to recreate the workspaces of 19th-century sculptors, bringing their legacies back into focus.

Prune Nourry

Throughout the late 19th and early 20th centuries, talented female sculptors lived and worked across Paris. Despite social constraints and limited access to artistic training, these pioneers made their mark in a predominantly male art world. Yet for a long time, women appeared in art history primarily as models or muses, while their roles as active artists were pushed into the background.

On October 20, a new exhibition titled "Visionaries" opens at the Petit Palais in Paris, coinciding with Art Basel Paris. The exhibition presents monumental plaster portraits sculpted by Prune Nourry, celebrating 18 historical female sculptors and their creative legacies.

To expand on their lives, Prune and Google Arts & Culture collaborated with film director Vincent Lorca on a 10-minute documentary. The project builds on a year of research during which three art historians gathered letters, journals, and photographic portraits of women sculptors who lived and worked in Paris. Because few historical photos of their actual workspaces exist, Lynn Cherny, creative technologist-in-residence at the Google Arts & Culture Lab used Google’s generative AI and image editing models to bring to life the studios of sculptors like Nancy Elizabeth Prophet, Jane Poupelet, and Camille Claudel.

Using a custom tool built with Google Gemini, the team created 3D models from archival photos to animate camera paths, allowing viewers to move virtually through the historical studios.

In another sequence conceived by Prune and Lorca, AI image editing is used to make the female students slowly fade from an archival photograph of Antoine Bourdelle’s studio, leaving only the men. The effect visually demonstrates how these talented women vanished from history.

"Visionaries" runs at the Petit Palais from October 20, 2026, through January 30, 2027, alongside the film installation in the museum galleries and a behind-the-scenes trailer online on Google Arts & Culture.

To discover more stories of trailblazing women who have shaped global culture, explore more Google Arts & Culture initiatives, such as Surfacing Women in Smithsonian History with the Smithsonian, Road to Equality, Women in India: Unheard Stories, and the Artemisia Gentileschi retrospective.

我们与艺术家 Prune Nourry 合作拍摄了一部纪录片，利用 Google AI 重现19世纪雕塑家的工作空间，让她们留下的艺术遗产重新受到关注。

Prune Nourry

艺术家

Amit Sood

Google 艺术与文化副总裁

在19世纪末至20世纪初，才华横溢的女性雕塑家在巴黎各处生活和工作。尽管受到社会约束，接受艺术训练的机会也有限，这些先驱仍在男性主导的艺术界留下了自己的印记。然而，长期以来，女性在艺术史中主要以模特或缪斯的身份出现，而她们作为艺术创作者的角色却被淡化。

10月20日，名为“远见者”的新展览在巴黎小皇宫开幕，与巴黎巴塞尔艺术展同期举行。展览呈现了 Prune Nourry 创作的巨型石膏肖像雕塑，致敬18位历史上的女性雕塑家及其创作遗产。

为更深入地讲述她们的生平，Prune 与 Google 艺术与文化携手电影导演 Vincent Lorca，合作拍摄了一部10分钟的纪录片。该项目以为期一年的研究为基础，期间三位艺术史学家收集了曾在巴黎生活和工作的女性雕塑家的书信、日记和肖像照片。由于记录她们实际工作空间的历史照片寥寥无几，Google 艺术与文化实验室的驻留创意技术专家 Lynn Cherny 利用 Google 的生成式 AI 和图像编辑模型，生动重现了 Nancy Elizabeth Prophet、Jane Poupelet 和 Camille Claudel 等雕塑家的工作室。

团队使用基于 Google Gemini 构建的定制工具，根据档案照片创建3D模型，并制作摄像机运动路径动画，让观众能够以虚拟方式穿行于这些历史上的工作室。

在 Prune 和 Lorca 构思的另一段影像中，AI 图像编辑技术让 Antoine Bourdelle 工作室的一张档案照片中的女学生逐渐淡去，最终只留下男性。这一效果直观地展现了这些才华横溢的女性如何从历史中消失。

“远见者”展览将于2026年10月20日至2027年1月30日在小皇宫举行，同期还将在博物馆展厅内呈现影像装置，并在 Google 艺术与文化网站上发布幕后预告片。

如想了解更多塑造了全球文化的女性先驱的故事，请探索 Google 艺术与文化的更多项目，例如与史密森学会合作的发掘史密森学会历史中的女性、平等之路、印度女性：未被听见的故事，以及Artemisia Gentileschi 回顾展。
